title: Prompt Refinement Round 2B (FINAL Dataset V1 prompt iteration)

checkpoint_status.claim_discipline: Round 2A causally demonstrated that changing rubric communication changes model behaviour. Round 2B demonstrated that a smaller, targeted prompt can materially improve qwen3.8-max on Dataset V1 (+0.084 Macro F1). NOT claimed: prompt is the sole bottleneck; prompt is the dominant cause of all matcher errors; Dataset V1 gains prove generalisation; qwen3.8-max + Prompt C is production-proven. The +0.084 development-set improvement MUST be validated on held-out Dataset V2.

purpose: Test whether a SMALLER rubric-aligned prompt (Prompt C) retains the useful Round 2A gains without the regressions of the full Prompt B. FINAL allowed iterative prompt-development round on Dataset V1.
prompt_b_rejected: job-fit-v3-rubric-aligned-v1 (Round 2A; 5 rule groups incl. OR-list + compound)
prompt_c_refined: job-fit-v3-rubric-refined-v2 (Round 2B; 3 compact rule groups: Technology Adjacency + Project-vs-Formal-Work + Strong/Partial/Missing Calibration ONLY)
prompt_c_rules_kept: A. Technology Adjacency — adjacent tech is not automatic Partial; general AI/LLM/RAG is not automatic credit for multimodal / ASR / RL-training / fine-tuning / training-infra / specialised rec-search; general-or-neighbouring-only -> Missing.

B. Project vs Formal Work Experience — a direct and complete project may support Strong for practical / implementation / delivery / productisation / hands-on requirements; when formal professional-role experience / job-function years / seniority / tenure / ownership scope is explicitly requested, project alone is not equivalent — Partial at most.

C. Strong / Partial / Missing Calibration — Strong = direct sufficiently-complete at the requested level; Partial = meaningful but materially incomplete; Missing = no meaningful or only general/adjacent evidence; do not use Partial merely because the model is uncertain.
prompt_c_rules_removed_vs_b: OR / alternative-list rule — Round 2A mixed (Sonnet ++, qwen +, kimi-k3 materially REGRESSED on the OR-list slice). Finalists are kimi-k3 and qwen3.8-max; Prompt C is not optimised for Sonnet. REMOVED.
Compound requirement / narrowest-unmet-subclaim rule — Round 2A: compound slice REGRESSED for all three tested models. Rejected in its current wording. REMOVED.
no_new_rules: no OR replacement, no compound replacement, no examples, no few-shot, no Dataset V1 cases, no Ground Truth labels, no candidate/company guidance, no new scoring rules. Prompt C is a REDUCTION of Prompt B.
control_source: reused Round 1B same-contract results; NO control rerun
fixed_contract: Dataset V1, 30 jobs, 100 matchable requirements, Ground Truth V2, frozen candidate evidence, Section D 4-field output contract, TRANSPORT_NORMALIZATION_MAPPING, one call/job, join key (job_id, requirement_id), _normalize_matches, MatchScoreService, transport, reasoning mode, temperature, max_tokens=4096. ONLY the instruction block changed. Raw persisted before GT load (guard GROUND_TRUTH_NOT_LOADED_YET on all 60 records).

prompt_bottleneck_status: REAL_BUT_PARTIAL_LEVER (Round 2A causally demonstrated rubric communication affects behaviour; NOT the sole/dominant cause; no ~93%-causal claim). Round 2B refines that: for qwen3.8-max the refined prompt yields a large development-set gain; for kimi-k3 any added rubric block is net-negative.

B_full_rubric.note: REJECTED — 1-job coverage failure; OR-list slice regressed

kimi-k3.verdict: Prompt C RESTORED full coverage (100/100, the Round 2A failure did NOT recur) and pushed Partial precision above 0.60 (0.609), but Macro F1 REGRESSED -0.017 (0.740 -> 0.7225): the explicit rules over-push kimi-k3 toward Strong (Strong recall 0.83 -> 0.90) and collapse Partial recall (0.567 -> 0.467). kimi-k3's calibration was already good; any added rubric block destabilises its Partial/Strong boundary, and its OR-list slice stays below control even without the OR-list rule.
kimi-k3.kimi_decision_rule: prefer C over control ONLY if coverage=100/100 AND ECC>=0.74 AND Macro F1>=0.740 AND grounding not degraded

qwen3.8-max.verdict: Prompt C is a LARGE development-set win for qwen3.8-max: Macro F1 +0.084 (0.702 -> 0.786), ECC +0.07 (0.71 -> 0.78), Partial precision 0.512 -> 0.643 (crosses 0.60 — first config in the whole benchmark to do so, together with kimi-k3 C), Missing recall 0.556 -> 0.889, Strong->Partial 13 -> 8, Missing->Partial 8 -> 2, Match-Score MAE 11.5 -> 7.5, score-vs-HMF 0.609 -> 0.704, Chinese-JD Macro F1 +0.052 — all with 100/100 coverage, grounding 1.0/0.0 preserved, and only +9% tokens (Prompt C is half the size of Prompt B). The REDUCED prompt beat the full Prompt B (+0.072) decisively, indicating the OR-list and compound rules in B were confusing/counterproductive for qwen3.8-max.
qwen3.8-max.qwen_decision_rule: prefer C over control if coverage=100/100 AND ECC>=0.71 AND Macro F1 improves meaningfully AND grounding not degraded

monitoring_slices_after_removing_rules.or_list: kimi-k3: still below control (mF1 0.736 -> 0.630) even though the OR-list RULE was removed — kimi's OR-list handling degrades under ANY added rubric block, not the OR-list rule specifically. qwen3.8-max: fine (0.458 -> 0.521), no regression from removing the rule.
monitoring_slices_after_removing_rules.compound: kimi-k3: RESTORED to control (mF1 0.626 -> 0.626) after removing the compound rule. qwen3.8-max: still below control (0.627 -> 0.510) — this is dataset difficulty on the compound slice, present even with no compound rule; not caused by Prompt C.

dataset_v2_finalists.reversal_note: This REVERSES the Round 1B/2A primary (kimi-k3). Under each model's FINAL Dataset V1 configuration, qwen3.8-max + Prompt C now leads on Macro F1 (0.786 vs 0.740), ECC (0.78 vs 0.74), and Chinese-JD (0.761 vs 0.752 ~ tied), and it is ~2.5x faster with no reasoning-mandatory / temperature=1 caveat. kimi-k3 retains only the score-vs-HMF-correlation edge (0.723 vs 0.704). The task's 'prefer Kimi as primary unless the refined experiment materially changes the quality/reliability conclusion' condition IS triggered: +0.046 Macro F1 and +0.04 ECC in qwen3.8-max's favour is material.
dataset_v2_finalists.caveat: qwen3.8-max's +0.084 gain is a DEVELOPMENT-SET result on the FINAL tuning iteration; the adjacency/project/calibration rules were shaped from Dataset V1 error analysis. The magnitude MUST be confirmed on held-out Dataset V2. kimi-k3 + control is the robust, un-tuned fallback if the qwen3.8-max gain does not hold on V2.

dataset_v1_stop_rule: MANDATORY. This is the FINAL Dataset V1 prompt-development iteration. NO Round 2C. NO further rule tuning against Dataset V1. NO more examples. NO further failure inspection + prompt iteration. Move to Dataset V2 held-out validation.
dataset_governance: Dataset V1 = development / model-selection / prompt-development data. NOT unbiased final evaluation. Dataset V2 = future held-out validation/test; NOT used in this task.
